Text: Andre Agassi escaped disaster on Thursday but Wimbledon finalist MaliVai Washington and Marcelo Rios were not so fortunate on a night of upsets at the U.S. Open. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: The 11th-seeded Washington fell short of reprising his Wimbledon miracle comeback as he lost to red-hot wildcard Alex O'Brien 6-3 6-4 5-7 3-6 6-3 in a two hour 51 minute struggle on the Stadium court. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Next door on the grandstand, 10th seed Rios lost to another player with a Wimbledon connection -- bad boy Jeff Tarango. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: But the night belonged to the upstarts. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Yeltsin endorses Lebed Chechnya peace plan - agency. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Friday that President Boris Yeltsin, who is vacationing outside Moscow, had backed security chief Alexander Lebed's peace plan for Chechnya, Interfax news agency said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Lebed, whom Yeltsin ordered to restore peace in Chechnya, struck a military deal with separatist rebels last week ending the worst fighting in the region in more than a year. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Chernomyrdin said on Thursday after a meeting with Lebed and top officials, who discussed Lebed's plans to restore peace in Chechnya, that it needed more work. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: "That's it, the war is over," Lebed told reporters who witnessed the signing. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: "Then, with cool heads, calmly and soberly we will sort out our relations," Lebed said after the late-night signing ceremony in this settlement outside Chechnya's eastern border. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Top Belarus politician blasts president. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Larisa Sayenko Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: MINSK 1996-08-30 Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: A senior Belarus politician accused President Alexander Lukashenko on Friday of attempting to set up a dictatorship in the former Soviet republic. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: The speaker of the Belarus parliament, Semyon Sharetsky, told Reuters that a draft constitution, due to be put to a national referendum on November 7, would dangerously increase the powers of the ruler. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: "The world community should not be indifferent to the fact that President Lukashenko, who leads this European state of 10 million people, is trying to establish a dictatorship with his new constitution," Sharetsky said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: The new constitution calls for a two-chamber parliament with a 110-seat majority-elected house of representatives and a regionally-represented senate with a third of its members named by the president. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Lukashenko's aides shrugged off Sharetsky's charge. " Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: If there was a dictatorship they wouldn't have the right to say things like this, "Sergei Posukhov, Lukashenko's political adviser, told Reuters. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Lukashenko, 41, won presidential polls in 1994 on promises to restore order, fight corruption and repair the strong links with Russia that were disrupted by the collapse of the Soviet Union. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: But during his period in office he has battled against nationalist opponents, trade unions and parliament and Sharetsky said the current parliament was ready to try to impeach him. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: "This constitution, which has been prepared in secret, aims to gather all power in one man's hands," he said. " Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: We should not be fooled by his quasi-democratic rhetoric and his methods, like this referendum. " Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Lukashenko signed a pact with Moscow in April to create a strong economic and political union which he believes could grow into a federation. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: But nationalist groups, scared by the prospect of renewed Moscow domination and Russia's backing for Lukashenko, protested against the deal. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: South Africa managed to avoid a fifth successive defeat in 1996 at the hands of the All Blacks with an emphatic 32-22 victory in front of an ecstatic Ellis Park crowd on Saturday. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: They scored three tries in recording their highest total against New Zealand, salvaging some pride in a season in which the world champions have lost five out of eight tests. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: It also ended a run of nine successive victories this year for New Zealand but arrived too late to prevent a 2-1 series defeat and an historic first All Black series triumph on South African soil. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Fullback Andre Joubert scored the other, scorching in from 40 metres at the start of the second half to add to his three long-range penalties. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: The All Blacks salvaged some pride by scoring two tries from centre Walter Little and scrum-half Justin Marshall in the final five minutes to close a gap which at one point stood at 24 points. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: But they generally endured an off-day, highlighted by recalled fly-half Andrew Mehrtens who missed five out of eight kicks at goal. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Recalled fly-half Henry Honiball kicked the Springboks into a 6-0 lead after 10 minutes only to see Andrew Mehrtens launch a penalty from eight metres inside his own half to narrow the gap. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Mehrtens missed three further penalties and a conversion in the first 40 minutes which could have put his side ahead, but it was the Springboks who looked the more dangerous. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Their promise was realised when Joubert made a 40-metre break in the 25th minute and, although winger Pieter Hendriks appeared to knock on Joubert's reverse pass, Welsh referee Derek Bevan allowed Van der Westhuizen to pick up and score under the posts. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Honiball converted and Joubert kicked a penalty before All Black hooker Sean Fitzpatrick scored a try from close range on the stroke of half-time to narrow the lead to 16-8 and hint at a comeback. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Instead Joubert kicked another long penalty and then raced around the outside of the defence to score the Springboks' second try. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: A quick penalty from Van der Westhuizen five metres from the All Black line set up the third try for Venter five minutes later and when Joubert kicked his third penalty the Springboks held an unassailable 32-8 lead going into the last quarter. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: When the All Blacks did break through, it was too late. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Centre Walter Little followed up Mehrtens' kick to score under the posts and scrum-half Justin Marshall forced himself over from a ruck close to the line in injury-time to give them some consolation. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Controversial IRA film screened at Venice festival. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Vera Haller Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: VENICE, Italy 1996-08-31 Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Dublin-born director Neil Jordan says he never lost more sleep over a film than over "Michael Collins", his controversial epic about the IRA which has its premiere on Saturday at the Venice Film Festival. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: The film, starring Liam Neeson and Julia Roberts, recounts the life of Michael Collins, the Irish Republican Army's Director of Intelligence who fought for Irish independence from 1919 to 1921. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Although not due for release in Britain until early next year, some politicians have already said they feared it would fan sectarian tensions in British-ruled Northern Ireland. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Jordan defends his decision to make the film, whose screenplay he wrote himself after years of research, saying it was "more about history than any political statement". Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: "The film spares neither the Irish nor the British in its depiction of the savagery of the time," Jordan said in a statement released by Warner Bros. " Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: How often has independence been achieved without bloodshed? Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Very rarely. " Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Jordan, whose 1992 film "The Crying Game" also came under fire for what was perceived as a sympathetic portrayal of the IRA, said Collins was more than just a revolutionary. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: "He developed techniques of guerilla warfare later copied by independence movements around the world, from Mao Tse-Tung in China to Yitzak Shamir in Israel," Jordan said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: "Collins would never be a proponent of contemporary terrorism as practised today. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: He was a soldier and a statesman and, over time, a man of peace. " Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Leeson, the Northern Ireland-born actor who was nominated for an Oscar for best actor for his performance in "Schindler's List", plays the lead role in Jordan's film. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Aidan Quinn portrays Harry Boland, Collins' best friend, and rival for the love of Kitty Kiernan, played by Roberts. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: Much of the film was shot on location in Dublin with Jordan using thousands of its citizens as unpaid extras. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: A set, however, was used for the fighting scenes. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: Noting that information about Collins was "as mysterious as the existence he maintained", Jordan said he made some historical assumptions in the film. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: "I have made choices about certain events based on my own extensive research into his letters and reported speeches," he said. " Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: I wanted to make this a story as accurate as possible without killing it dramatically and I think I have. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: It is a very true film. " Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: One of the assumptions is his interpretation of the murky circumstances surrounding the shooting death of Collins, who had broken with his comrades when he sought a negotiated settlement with Britain, in an ambush in 1922. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:

Text: "I have never lost more sleep over the making of a film than I have over' Michael Collins', but I'll never make a more important one," Jordan said. Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
Text: "In the life of one person you can tell the events that formed the north and south of Ireland as they are today." Following the entity order: first to last Entities:
